Memory/Public/Learnings/WhatsAppSetup.title: Meta WhatsApp Business Setup
Memory/Public/Learnings/WhatsAppSetup.content:
Meta WhatsApp Business API Setup
Learn how to set up WhatsApp messaging for church services.
📋 Prerequisites

Meta Business Account
WhatsApp Business Account
Developer Portal Access

🚀 Step-by-Step Setup
1. Create Meta Developer Account

Go to developers.facebook.com
Click “My Apps” → “Create App”
Select “Other” → “Business”
Fill in app details

2. Setup WhatsApp Product

In your app dashboard
Add “WhatsApp” product
Get Phone Number ID
Get WhatsApp Business Account ID

3. Get Access Token

Settings → WhatsApp → Configuration
Generate temporary access token
Note the token expiry time

4. Setup Webhook

Configure webhook URL
Verify webhook secret
Subscribe to events:

messages
message_sent
message_delivered



📱 Sending Messages
Using cURL
curl -X POST 'graph.facebook.com/v21.0/PHONE_NUMBER_ID/messages' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
    "to": "RECIPIENT_PHONE",
    "type": "text",
    "text": {"body": "Hello!"}
  }'
Using Node.js
const axios = require('axios');
 
async function sendMessage(phoneNumberId, to, message) {
  await axios.post(
    `graph.facebook.com/v21.0/${phoneNumberId}/messages`,
    {
      messaging_product: "whatsapp",
      to: to,
      type: "text",
      text: { body: message }
    },
    {
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
      }
    }
  );
}
📝 Message Templates
Templates must be approved by Meta:

Use meaningful variables: {{1}}, {{2}}
Keep under character limits
Include opt-out option for marketing

🔐 Security Best Practices

Store tokens in environment variables
Use webhooks for verification
Validate incoming messages
Rate limiting

🐛 Common Issues





















ErrorSolutionToken expiredRegenerate in dashboardPhone not verifiedComplete business verificationRate limitImplement backoff

README.content:
Welcome to Quartz
This is your digital garden built with Quartz.
Getting Started

Add markdown files to the content folder
Run npx quartz build to build the site
Run npx quartz serve to preview locally

Memory Structure
content/
├── Memory/
│   ├── Private/    # Private notes (not published)
│   └── Public/     # Public notes (published to git)

Notes

Files in Private folder can be excluded from publishing
Use frontmatter to control visibility
Quartz supports Obsidian-flavored markdown
